claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure consisting of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The starting alloy exhibits limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittle behavior.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal phase boundaries cause local stress concentrations, microcracking, and brittle failure in the starting alloy.
The proposed compositional intervention is the addition of 1–2 at.% tungsten.
The proposed thermal intervention is solutionizing at approximately 1000°C for 1 hour followed by aging at approximately 600°C for 5 hours.
The tungsten addition and heat treatment will produce coherent nanometric tungsten-rich precipitates.
The tungsten-rich precipitates will preferentially localize at lamellar colony boundaries.
Tungsten promotes the nucleation of fine coherent precipitates during aging.
The coherent precipitates act as dislocation-pinning sites.
Precipitate-mediated pinning reduces dislocation accumulation near lamellar interfaces.
Reducing dislocation accumulation lowers local stress concentrations and delays microcrack initiation during tensile deformation.
The precipitates provide additional precipitation strengthening.
The treatment will significantly increase room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment will maintain or slightly increase tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
Excessive tungsten or non-optimal aging could cause over-precipitation and embrittlement.
The proposed beneficial mechanism is expected to apply only at room temperature under quasi-static loading.
